rules.what: Circular dependency detected between layers. Each layer must only depend on layers below it.
rules.why: Circular dependencies make the codebase untestable, fragile, and hard to reason about. Clean layered architecture requires acyclic dependency graphs.
rules.fix: Break the cycle by introducing an interface/abstraction in the lower layer, or extract shared types to a common module that both layers can depend on.

rules.description: Domain layer has no external dependencies
rules.what: Domain layer imports from infrastructure, presentation, or application layer. Domain must be pure and dependency-free.
rules.why: The domain layer contains core business logic. External dependencies on frameworks, databases, or UI layers make it non-portable and hard to test.
rules.fix: Move infrastructure-specific code to the infrastructure layer. Use dependency inversion: define interfaces in domain, implement them in infrastructure.

rules.what: Presentation layer directly imports from infrastructure layer. Use the application layer as intermediary.
rules.why: Direct infrastructure access from the UI creates tight coupling. The application layer should orchestrate infrastructure access, keeping the presentation layer thin.
rules.fix: Create an application-layer service/facade that wraps the infrastructure call, and have the presentation layer use that instead.
